title: UCAD main-chain report
description: The document `node scripts/verify-main-chain.mjs --report <file>` writes on a machine that ran steps 1-5, and the document `--judge <file>` reads back. This file is the shape, not the verdict: it says which fields a report has and what type each one is. Whether a report closes the Windows row is decided by `judgeReport()` in `scripts/verify-main-chain.mjs`, which validates against this schema first and then asks the questions a schema cannot: is `platform` the platform the row is about, is `build.version` this repository's version, is every driven step present and `pass`, and does every `pass` carry an evidence line the step recorded. A report that does not match this shape is not judged further — the shape is the precondition for every other question.

platform.description: `process.platform` of the machine that ran the steps. The Windows row needs `win32`; a report from another platform is a real result about that platform, and `judgeReport()` refuses it by name rather than reading it as a Windows run.

build.description: Which build was measured. Only the two fields the judgement reads are required: `executable` (what was launched) and `version` (what `judgeReport()` compares against this repository). `sizeBytes` and `modifiedAt` are declared but optional — they are what a reader uses to tell two runs of the same path apart, and `buildReport()` always writes them, but no verdict depends on them. Every field but `executable` may be null: this is a description, not a check.

executable.description: Absolute path of the executable that was launched.

version.description: The version in `package.json` at the time of the run. `judgeReport()` compares it against this repository's version: a report about another build proves something about another build.

sizeBytes.description: Size of the executable in bytes, or null when it could not be read.

modifiedAt.description: ISO-8601 mtime of the executable, or null when it could not be read.

ranAt.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of the run. Not judged — it is what a reader uses to tell two reports apart.

steps.description: One row per step the script can drive, not only the ones this run was asked for: a partial run (`--steps 1,4`) has to read as "2, 3 and 5 were not covered" rather than as a report that happens to have two rows.

n.description: The step number, 1-5. Step 6 is the five fixture states a person walks by eye under `npm run dev:web`; no report closes it.

verdict.description: `pass` and `fail` are the run's own. `skip` is a step the run was not asked for, kept rather than dropped so a reader comparing two reports sees what the second one did not cover. A step that was asked for and reached neither verdict is written as `fail`.

evidence.description: The lines the step recorded, as `<n>:<key>=<value>`. Never empty: a step with nothing to say gets a sentence saying so, because an empty list reads as "nothing to say". `judgeReport()` does not count that sentence as evidence — a `pass` with nothing behind it is a claim, not a result.

note.description: The report's own statement of what it is: a record of what a run printed, which cannot prove the steps were performed on the machine `platform` names. Written by `buildReport()` so a reader who never opens the script still knows what they are holding.
